surface: GET /api/verify-signal?hash=<signal_hash> (the form baked into every webhook verify_url) — dual with the existing ?signalId=<int>
serving: Caddy proxies /api/verify-signal → app:3000. The /verify landing page (static, Caddy file_server) reads ?hash= and calls this endpoint. R2 (Mr.1-ratified): no Caddyfile change.
naming_law: public response uses calls-language; verdict surfaced as both `call` (NAMING-LAW) and `direction` (existing render-compat); price as both `price_at_call` and `price`. `signal_hash` kept (existing identifier).

pending_200.when: call recorded but not yet in a Merkle batch

forbidden_key_rationale: Phase-E internal outcome metrics (Data Integrity LAW). getSignalByHash's SELECT is the allow-list — it never projects these even when the underlying signals row has them populated (asserted by tests/verify-hash.test.ts).
existing_path_invariant: GET /api/verify-signal?signalId=<int> response is byte-for-byte unchanged (signal:{id,coin,direction,confidence,timeframe,price,timestamp,hash}); only the new ?hash= branch adds call/exchange/regime/price_at_call.
drift_check_command: BAD=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'https://algovault.com/api/verify-signal?hash=nothex'); test "$BAD" = 400 || { echo "MALFORMED_NOT_400: $BAD"; exit 1; }; UNK="0x$(printf 'f%.0s' $(seq 1 64))"; test "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://algovault.com/api/verify-signal?hash=$UNK")" = 404 || { echo 'UNKNOWN_NOT_404'; exit 1; }; curl -s "https://algovault.com/api/verify-signal?hash=$UNK" | jq -e '[paths(scalars)|map(tostring)|join(".")]|map(select(test("outcome_|pfe_|mae_|return_pct_|price_after_")))|length==0' >/dev/null || { echo 'INTERNAL_FIELD_LEAKED_IN_ERROR_BODY'; exit 1; }; echo SHAPE_OK
drift_check_note: SEC-42 (OPS-AUDIT-REMEDIATION-LOW-W2). The prior command was broken three ways and could assert nothing: `H=$(curl ... >/dev/null; echo 0x...)` discarded the fetch and assigned the literal string '0x...', H was then never used, the URL interpolated an UNDEFINED $KNOWN_HASH, and the 'assert' was a prose `echo`. SCOPE, stated honestly rather than faked: the verified_200 path CANNOT be exercised by a drift check — `signal_hash` is delivered to consumers in webhook payloads and is exposed by NO public read endpoint (probed 2026-08-02: /api/merkle-batches returns batch_id/merkle_root/tx_hash but no per-signal hash, and /api/recent-calls carries no hash). A first attempt at this command used `.batches[0].signals[0].hash` and returned NO_HASH_AVAILABLE on its first verbatim run, which is exactly why the contract requires running it. So the check asserts the three things that ARE publicly assertable and load-bearing: malformed hash -> 400, unknown well-formed hash -> 404, and NO internal field (outcome_/pfe_/mae_/return_pct_/price_after_) appears anywhere in the error body (recursive over paths, not just top level). The 200-shape allow-list remains documented in `responses.verified_200` for review, unasserted by design.
projection_note: SEC-42 (OPS-AUDIT-REMEDIATION-LOW-W2): build-knowledge-json.mjs reads flat `snapshot_date` / `endpoint` / `allowed_keys` (Array) with a TOTAL per-field fallback. This file kept its date as `captured_at` and its allow-list NESTED per-response/per-section, so the public bundle advertised snapshot_date:'unknown', the FILENAME as the endpoint, and allowed_keys:[] — a meaningless shape contract — with a green build. Flat canonical keys added (allowed_keys = the union across all four response states); the nested `responses` structure is retained as the detailed source of truth.
